scenes.title: Deconstructing Standardized Variables d1 and d2

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down d2 and Probabilities: d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T), with N(d2) as exercise probability and N(d1) as Delta ([fact-03], [fact-04]).

summarySteps: 1. BSM European Call Formula ([fact-01]): c = S0 * N(d1) - K * exp(-r * T) * N(d2) represents expected present value of stock conditional on exercise minus strike present value.
2. BSM European Put Formula ([fact-02]): p = K * exp(-r * T) * N(-d2) - S0 * N(-d1), linked via Put-Call Parity.
3. Standardized Variables d1 and d2 ([fact-03]): Measure standard deviations of log strike from expected terminal stock price.
4. Probabilistic Meanings ([fact-04]): N(d2) is the exact risk-neutral exercise probability P(S_T > K), and N(d1) is the dynamic Delta hedge ratio dc/dS0.
5. Benchmark Example ([fact-05]): For S0 = $42, K = $40, r = 10%, sigma = 20%, T = 0.5, European call price is $4.76 and put price is $0.81.
6. Implied Volatility and VIX ([fact-06]): Volatility equating theoretical BSM price to market price, aggregated across 30-day S&P 500 options into the CBOE VIX Index.
7. Continuous Dividend Yields ([fact-07]): Stock discounted at expiration becomes S0 * exp(-q * T), generalizing BSM formulas and Put-Call Parity.

8. American Call Early Exercise & Net Profit ([fact-08], [fact-09]): American calls warrant early exercise before ex-dividend date t1 if D > K * [1 - exp(-r * (T - t1))], and net trading profit equals Gross Payoff minus Premium paid.
bottomTakeaway: The Black-Scholes-Merton model provides closed-form European option pricing through cumulative normal probabilities N(d1) and N(d2), governed by implied volatility and generalized for continuous dividend yields ([fact-01], [fact-04], [fact-06], [fact-07]).
